title: Workflow execution
explanation: The workflow steps that are fact-shaped: a conforming task, a resolved operation path, a known test tier, and a hermetic test. The facts come from the task and test extractors.

cases.original: Execute only a conforming task; report a malformed one instead of guessing what it meant.
cases.note: The extractor reports whether the task conforms; the rule refuses a malformed one. What counts as malformed is the extractor's definition, not the engine's.
cases.suggestion: Name the sections a task must have, so conformance is a checklist.

cases.original: For a `modify`, `delete`, or `rename` operation, verify that the referenced path exists or report that it is missing.
cases.note: A missing path is emitted as a finding, not a refusal; the task decides what to do.
cases.suggestion: Keep the three verbs in one list; say whether a missing path stops the task.

cases.original: Classify every test into one tier:
cases.note: The rule checks that the tier is one the project defines; whether the classification is right is a review.
cases.suggestion: List the allowed tiers in one sentence the extractor can read.

cases.original: A test never touches the real system: sandbox `HOME` and XDG paths into a temporary directory, serve HTTP on `127.0.0.1`, and use no outside network.
cases.note: The extractor reports whether the test is hermetic; the specific isolation mechanisms are not each checked.
cases.suggestion: Say "a test declares itself hermetic and names its isolation mechanism".
